### Summary

- Cache successful Claude CLI version probes for 30 minutes.
- Invalidate immediately when the resolved executable fingerprint changes.
- Coalesce concurrent probes without retaining nonzero, timed-out, empty, or thrown results.
- Keep real installed-CLI probing explicit through `LIVE_CLAUDE_TTY=1`.

### Maintainer hardening

- Replaced the unbounded fingerprint dictionary with one bounded cache entry.
- Added TTL refresh for stable wrapper paths whose target may change without wrapper metadata changing.
- Require a successful exit status before accepting output as a version.
- Reject negative cache ages after wall-clock rollback and sample cache time inside the lock.
- Added deterministic coverage for failure retry, deadline retry, TTL expiry, clock rollback, fingerprint invalidation, and concurrent single-flight behavior.

### Verification

- `swift test --filter ProviderVersionDetectorTests`: 16 tests, 1 explicit live-test skip, 0 failures.
- `make test`: 638 selections across 54 groups, 0 failures or retries.
- `make check`: clean.
- Autoreview: clean after two concurrency/time-edge fixes.

The live installed-Claude proof remains available with `LIVE_CLAUDE_TTY=1 swift test --filter ProviderVersionDetectorTests/test_claudeVersion_realExecutableProof`; it is opt-in to avoid unexpected PTY/account interaction in ordinary test runs.

target.title: Add shareable subscription usage cards
target.body:
## Product case

CodexBar already computes local token and estimated-cost history, but the menu is a poor sharing surface: the numbers cannot be copied as one artifact, and a menu screenshot is fragile and difficult to read. This PR turns the existing local data into a fixed 1200x630 card plus a plain-text equivalent.

The intentionally narrow v1 is **local export**, not a hosted profile:

- no account system, public URL, upload, tracking, or backend;
- no prompt, project, path, email, or account identity in the payload;
- no attempt to make unlike measurements look complete; unknown spend remains unknown;
- one immutable payload drives preview, PNG, clipboard text, and saved image.

Alternatives considered:

- **Screenshot the current menu:** clips, changes size, and mixes controls with the artifact.
- **Hosted share link / OG page:** introduces persistence, deletion, abuse, and privacy-policy work that is not justified for v1.
- **Provider-by-provider exports:** fails the core use case of comparing all enabled AI subscriptions in one picture.

## What this adds

- A native **Share Stats...** action in the status menu and Settings -> Menu -> Sharing.
- A 1200x630 local card with combined 30-day tracked tokens and estimated spend.
- Distinct ranked subscription rows with readable inline plan names and a three-model ranking.
- A ten-bucket activity strip whose colors reinforce the named subscription rows.
- OpenRouter API-key spend surfaced as explicitly labeled month-to-date data rather than hidden or mixed into the trailing-period total.
- **Copy Image**, **Copy Stats**, and **Save...** actions from one preview.
- Existing CodexBar typography, localization patterns, menu descriptors, and lifecycle handling.

## Permission and prompt boundary

The feature adds no entitlement, system permission request, network request, background upload, or automatic pasteboard write.

| User action | Side effect |
| --- | --- |
| Open Share Stats | Reads in-memory provider snapshots and configured local Codex history only. No prompt is presented. |
| Copy Image | Writes PNG/TIFF data to the pasteboard after the explicit button press. |
| Copy Stats | Writes plain text to the pasteboard after the explicit button press. |
| Save... | Presents the standard save panel only after the explicit button press. |

Sibling Codex-account history uses the account homes already represented in CodexBar settings. A missing, unreadable, or timed-out history source degrades to an unpriced connected row; the sharing flow does not request broad filesystem access to compensate.

## Account-complete data contract

| Surface | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Tracked tokens | Sum of known local token-history snapshots in the selected 30-day window. |
| Estimated spend | Sum of finite priced history only; the card reports priced-source coverage. |
| Codex subscriptions | One identity-free row per visible Codex account, labeled `Codex · #1`, `Codex · #2`, etc. |
| Other subscriptions | One row per enabled provider source. Missing local history reads `connected`, never `$0`. |
| OpenRouter spend | Uses the existing in-memory `keyUsageMonthly` value, labels it `MTD`, and reports it separately from trailing-30-day totals. |
| Top models | Cross-provider aggregation of real model breakdowns or model names for the same window; each row names its provider. |
| Activity strip | Tracked tokens grouped into at most ten time buckets and stacked by named subscription. |

The active Codex account reuses the normal provider snapshot. Each sibling account scans its own Codex home into a separate hashed cache, with Pi session history disabled for sibling scans so shared Pi history is counted exactly once. Account scan failures degrade to connected/unpriced rows rather than deleting a visible subscription.

## Readability and accessibility

- The card is designed and checked at its 600 x 315 feed render, not only at the 1200 x 630 export size.
- Essential labels start at 18 pt native; subscription and model names use 20 pt. Tiny plan pills and model-mapping microcopy were removed.
- Every provider and model association uses a name and two-digit rank in addition to a compact color locator.
- Against the warm near-black background, primary text measures 16.5:1, secondary text 8.1:1, and the OpenRouter accent 7.8:1.
- The exported artifact is static and does not depend on motion or hover state.
- The sourced standards, Exa/Parallel comparison, and OpenRouter frontier-model panel are documented in [the readability review](docs/share-card-readability-review-2026-07-13.md).

## Privacy allowlist

The export payload permits provider display name, plan label, aggregate tokens, aggregate estimated cost, active-day counts, model name, period end, and per-subscription daily aggregate token counts. It does not carry email, account ID, project name/path, prompt text, session title, file content, credentials, or raw event records. Rendering and pasteboard/save operations are local.

## Current configured-bundle proof

These images come from a freshly compiled, signed local app bundle using the contributor's real configured aggregate data. The payload contains no account identity, prompts, projects, paths, endpoints, or credentials.

![Current real-bundle share card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/codex/shareable-usage-card/docs/screenshots/share-stats-real-bundle.png)

![Current real-bundle preview after Copy Image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/codex/shareable-usage-card/docs/screenshots/share-stats-real-preview.png)

Observed behavior:

- The production preview surfaced four named subscriptions, three named models, a 30-day estimate, and a separate OpenRouter MTD figure.
- Clicking the preview's real **Copy Image** action produced a 1200 x 630 pasteboard item with `public.png` and `public.tiff` representations; the preview status changed to `Image copied`.
- Clicking **Copy Stats** produced 610 characters containing the live subscription names, model-provider mappings, OpenRouter MTD amount, and local-generation provenance.
- No screen-recording permission was granted or required. The proof image was recovered from CodexBar's own clipboard export path.

## Relationship to the Settings dashboard

- Companion PR: [#2116 - Settings: add unified usage and spend dashboard](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2116)
- This PR owns the share/export workflow only.
- #2116 owns persistent in-app exploration only.
- Neither branch depends on the other at build or runtime.

## Verification

- [x] Incremental arm64 release build after the feed-readability redesign
- [x] Exact 1200 x 630 production view exported and visually inspected at both native and 600 x 315 feed size
- [x] Real configured-bundle Copy Image and Copy Stats paths exercised through the preview controls
- [x] Primary, secondary, and accent contrast measured at 16.5:1, 8.1:1, and 7.8:1
- [x] No new entitlement, dependency, network path, or automatic pasteboard behavior
- [ ] Real configured-bundle Save... confirmation
- [x] `swift test --filter ShareStatsTests` - 8 focused tests passed
- [x] `make check` - localization, formatting, SwiftLint, shell/docs/package gates passed
- [x] Fresh sharded test suite in GitHub CI

The local widget-packaging step is blocked by an installed Xcode `IDESimulatorFoundation` / `DVTDownloads` plug-in mismatch. This is machine-local; the CodexBar target builds cleanly, and GitHub CI is the authoritative full-suite result. The focused share-stat suite passes locally, including privacy-label and shared-calendar-window regressions. GitHub CI remains the authoritative full-suite result.

## Product/design decision requested

`VISION.md` requires sign-off for new product surfaces. This PR asks maintainers to approve a permanent, privacy-first local usage-card export that includes every visible subscription without exposing account identity or adding permission prompts.

target.title: fix: clear inherited signal masks for spawned CLIs
target.body:
## Summary

- Clear the inherited per-thread signal mask for both pipe and PTY children launched by `SpawnedProcessGroup`.
- Add a regression test that blocks `SIGTERM` in the parent thread and verifies that a spawned child starts with it unblocked.

This is a follow-up to #1883 and #2012. The transport fallback added there is present in 0.42.1, but authenticated Kiro CLI refreshes can still time out because `posix_spawn` inherits the calling Swift worker thread's blocked signal mask unless `POSIX_SPAWN_SETSIGMASK` is set explicitly.

## Root cause

On affected launches, the Kiro child inherited a non-empty signal mask from the Swift worker thread. Both the pipe attempt and its PTY fallback therefore reached the shared CodexBar deadline even though the same authenticated Kiro CLI command completed normally when run directly.

A shell wrapper appeared to fix the problem because the shell normalizes its signal state before `exec`. A controlled native launcher isolated that behavior:

| Native launcher behavior | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Inherit mask and dispositions | Timeout (~22 s) |
| Reset dispositions only | Timeout (~22 s) |
| Clear signal mask only | Success (~4 s) |

The fix supplies an empty `sigset_t` with `posix_spawnattr_setsigmask` and enables `POSIX_SPAWN_SETSIGMASK` for both launch paths.

## Authenticated reproduction and validation

All live output below was reduced to provider/version and boolean presence checks; no identity, account, or usage values are included.

Tested against upstream `main` at `9c3e09870b5e5ecea23d6fb998f31aaf23f84b54`, Kiro CLI 2.12.1, and the released CodexBar 0.42.1 (build 103). The release bundle identifies commit `7db921fe4`, which contains #2012.

| Machine | Released 0.42.1, no workaround | Patched `main`, no workaround |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MacBook (arm64) | Timeout (~21-22 s) | 3/3 successful: 4 s, 4 s, 3 s |
| Mac mini (arm64) | Timeout (~22 s) | 3/3 successful: 4 s, 3 s, 4 s |

Every patched run returned provider `kiro`, CLI version `2.12.1`, a populated usage payload, and Kiro-specific usage data. Both three-run series ended with zero residual Kiro processes.

Manual PTY invocation of the same authenticated Kiro CLI completed in about 3 seconds on both machines, which rules out credentials or provider availability as the cause.

## Checks

- `swift build --product CodexBarCLI` passes on both Macs.
- `swiftc -parse Tests/CodexBarTests/SpawnedProcessGroupTests.swift` passes.
- SwiftFormat lint: 0 of 1,426 files require formatting.
- Live authenticated Kiro matrix: 6/6 patched runs pass across two Macs; zero residual Kiro processes.
- Focused unit test is included, but cannot be executed locally because both hosts only have Command Line Tools; SwiftPM stops before test compilation because `actool` requires full Xcode.
- SwiftLint likewise cannot load `sourcekitdInProc.framework` from the Command Line Tools-only environment. CI should provide the full Xcode validation for both checks.

## Scope

The change is intentionally limited to process spawn attributes and one regression test. No Kiro-specific parsing, deadlines, credentials, or usage data are changed.

target.title: fix: Linux SIGILL during timezone resolution on non-FHS systems (fixes #2127)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #2127.

- Bootstrap timezone discovery before the Linux CLI enters Commander or other Foundation-dependent setup.
- When `TZ` is absent, require readable `/etc/localtime` whose resolved path contains a valid IANA `zoneinfo` identifier.
- Prime CoreFoundation with the actual timezone data, then expose the same IANA identifier to FoundationEssentials only after priming succeeds.
- Preserve every caller-provided `TZ` value and decline unsafe or unrecognized path fallbacks.
- Add focused pure-policy and Linux CoreFoundation bridge tests.

## Problem

On NixOS, `/etc/localtime` points into the Nix store and conventional `/usr/share/zoneinfo` paths may not exist. With `TZ` unset, Swift Foundation timezone conversion could terminate the CLI with `SIGILL` while constructing the default timezone.

The contributor reproduced this with both v0.42.1 x86_64 Linux artifacts and an unmodified `main` build. The repaired branch returned real Claude usage normally on that affected NixOS host.

## Fix

The Linux-only bootstrap runs at the start of `CodexBarCLI.main()`. It derives an IANA identifier only from a resolved `/zoneinfo/` path, rejects empty and traversal components, loads `/etc/localtime` data into CoreFoundation, and sets process-local `TZ` only when the bridge accepts that data.

No provider, authentication, account storage, parser, macOS, or system configuration behavior changes.

## Validation

- [x] Affected NixOS live before/after: v0.42.1 exited with SIGILL; repaired branch returned real Claude usage.
- [x] Linux Swift 6.2.1 container: `CLITimeZoneBootstrapTests`, 8 tests passed.
- [x] macOS focused suite: 7 applicable tests passed; Linux-only CoreFoundation integration is compile-time gated.
- [x] `make check`: SwiftFormat clean; SwiftLint 0 violations.
- [x] `make test`: 639 selections in 54 groups; 54 first-pass successes, zero retries or failures.
- [x] Maintainer autoreview: no accepted or actionable findings.
- [x] Exact-head x86_64 and arm64 musl static builds, smoke tests, and packages passed in https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/actions/runs/29287924777.

No UI changes; screenshots are not applicable.

target.title: Add ZenMux Management API provider
target.body:
## Summary

Adds ZenMux as a disabled-by-default API provider using the documented read-only Management API.

- Reads the rolling five-hour and seven-day quota windows from `GET /api/v1/management/subscription/detail`.
- Shows subscription tier, renewal date, non-healthy account status, reset countdowns, and compact used/max flow details.
- Enriches the snapshot with PAYG balance from `GET /api/v1/management/payg/balance`; a non-auth balance failure does not discard valid quota data.
- Renders PAYG balance as a compact credits row instead of exposing provider setup copy in the menu card.
- Accepts a ZenMux Management API key from provider config or `ZENMUX_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY`. Standard inference API keys are rejected with an actionable error.
- Wires provider registration, settings, CLI diagnostics, icon/widget exhaustiveness, cost-scan exclusion, docs, provider counts, and the generated social card.

## Security and privacy

- Requests are limited to the fixed `https://zenmux.ai/api/v1/management` origin and use the shared redirect-guarded transport.
- No endpoint override, browser cookie, dashboard session, inference prompt, or request log is read.
- Requests are timeout-bounded; cancellation is preserved, including during optional balance enrichment.
- ZenMux identity is provider-siloed and contains plan/status only; no identity is borrowed from another provider.

Official API references:

- https://docs.zenmux.ai/api/platform/subscription-detail
- https://docs.zenmux.ai/api/platform/payg-balance

## Validation

- `swift test --filter ZenMuxProviderTests`: 10/10 passed, including the final menu-card labels and layout model.
- `make check`: passed; SwiftFormat clean, SwiftLint 0 violations, generated parser hash/docs/locales/package gates current.
- `./Scripts/package_app.sh`: passed.
- Packaged `CodexBar.app` embeds exact commit `3a053d9f`; `codesign --verify --deep --strict CodexBar.app` passed.
- The exact-head packaged CLI completed an authenticated production Management API fetch. Redacted shape: both quota windows had numeric utilization/flow details and ISO-8601 reset timestamps; the subscription had an ISO-8601 renewal timestamp; PAYG returned a positive numeric credit balance. No key, account identifier, exact balance, or exact usage value is included here.

`make test` is not recorded as green: it discovered 639 selections in 54 groups, then stopped in group 3 after the untouched `AdaptiveRefreshTimerTests` race failed both the first pass and full-group retry. An isolated suite rerun reproduced the same existing timing behavior (`completedRefreshCountForTesting` became 2 instead of 1). No adaptive-refresh source or tests are changed by this PR.

## Redacted exact-head runtime proof

Validated July 13, 2026 using the packaged app from exact branch head `3a053d9f314d9cff443713bd8d4338f10178b5fe`:

```console
$ git rev-parse HEAD
3a053d9f314d9cff443713bd8d4338f10178b5fe

$ /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :CodexGitCommit" CodexBar.app/Contents/Info.plist
3a053d9f

$ codesign --verify --deep --strict CodexBar.app
# exit 0
```

The bundled CLI then completed a live authenticated Management API refresh. The following privacy projection was produced directly from that CLI JSON. It retains window lengths, field types, and presence checks while suppressing the API key, subscription tier, exact flow counts, utilization values, reset/renewal timestamps, and credit balance.

```json
{
  "provider": "zenmux",
  "source": "api",
  "usage": {
    "primary": {
      "windowMinutes": 300,
      "usedPercentType": "number",
      "resetTimestampPresent": true,
      "flowDetailPresent": true
    },
    "secondary": {
      "windowMinutes": 10080,
      "usedPercentType": "number",
      "resetTimestampPresent": true,
      "flowDetailPresent": true
    },
    "subscriptionTierPresent": true,
    "subscriptionRenewalTimestampPresent": true
  },
  "credits": {
    "remainingType": "number",
    "positiveBalancePresent": true
  }
}
```

This demonstrates that the live exact-head response populates the five-hour and weekly meters, both reset fields, compact flow details, subscription tier and renewal metadata, and the numeric PAYG balance consumed by the compact Credits row. Healthy account status is intentionally omitted by the UI; non-healthy statuses remain covered by focused presentation tests.

## Authenticated evidence

Exact-head live verification used a separately configured ZenMux Management API key. The key remained local and was never printed, committed, or passed to the PR. The packaged CLI confirmed both documented routes, quota reset timestamps, renewal mapping, flow details, and PAYG balance. The output above is intentionally shape-only to avoid publishing account telemetry.
